findings.title: Cancelling a transfer that is already gone (404) is reported as a service-unavailable error
findings.problem: cancel_download only accepts {200, 202, 204}. When slskd has already removed the transfer, it answers DELETE /transfers/downloads/{user}/{id} with 404, and the code then raises TransferEnqueueError(..., "unavailable"). A cancel exists to make the transfer stop; if the transfer is already gone, that goal is met. Reporting it as 'unavailable' leads callers to think slskd is down. They may then retry, surface a false failure, or leave the job stuck in a cancelling state. It also cannot be told apart from a real outage because it uses the same reason code. This can easily happen in practice: a transfer that completed or was removed between the poll and the cancel returns 404. pending: confirm slskd returns 404 for missing transfer ids (typical for its TransfersController) and how the upcoming active-cancellation caller (commit 1027691 tests) handles this error.
findings.fix_hint: treat 404 on cancel as idempotent success (or raise with a distinct reason like 'not_found') instead of 'unavailable'
findings.why_it_matters: A cancel race with transfer completion would be misreported as a slskd outage, causing wrong retry/failure handling.

members.title: Empty success_statuses set silently falls back to the {200, 201} default
members.problem: `success_statuses or {200, 201}` treats an explicitly passed empty set the same as None and replaces it with the default. No caller in this diff passes an empty set, so this is a latent footgun rather than an active bug.
members.why_it_matters: A caller that deliberately passes a set, such as one built from config, would get unexpected default acceptance semantics.
members.fix_hint: use `success_statuses if success_statuses is not None else {200, 201}`

members.title: Failed cancellations are raised as TransferEnqueueError with reason 'unavailable', which misclassifies them
members.problem: _request_json now serves DELETE as well, but every non-auth, non-5xx, unexpected-status failure (400, 404, 409) still raises TransferEnqueueError with reason 'unavailable'. A caller that catches TransferEnqueueError and assumes an enqueue failed, or that shows 'unavailable' to the operator, will misreport cancel failures.
source_window: f"slskd transfer request failed with HTTP {response.status_code}",
members.why_it_matters: Operators get the wrong diagnosis, and retry logic keyed on 'unavailable' may retry cancels that can never succeed.
members.fix_hint: Map 4xx client errors to a distinct reason (e.g. 'rejected'/'not_found') instead of 'unavailable'
